title: What If the Air Lost Its Oxygen for 5 Seconds?
description:
Oxygen is about 21% of the air we breathe. If it vanished for just five seconds, nothing could burn: every flame on Earth, from candles to gas stoves, would go out at once, and every petrol, diesel and jet engine would cut out, because they all burn fuel with oxygen from the air. Air pressure would also drop by about a fifth, roughly what you feel at 2,000 metres up a mountain, so everyone's ears would pop. Holding your breath for five seconds is easy, so most people would be fine.

Sources: NASA / NOAA composition of the atmosphere (nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%); US Standard Atmosphere (about 79 kPa at roughly 2 km).
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations. This is a thought experiment.
